headings.title: Introduction and Clinical Indications
headings.content: A sigmoidoscopy is a diagnostic endoscopic procedure that allows visualization of the interior of the rectum and the sigmoid colon. Utilizing a flexible or rigid tube equipped with a light and camera, healthcare providers can inspect the mucosal lining for abnormalities. This intervention is frequently utilized in Nigerian clinical practice for screening asymptomatic adults for colorectal cancer, investigating unexplained rectal bleeding, evaluating chronic diarrhea, and diagnosing inflammatory bowel disease such as ulcerative colitis.

headings.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Lower Bowel
headings.content: The sigmoid colon forms an S-shaped curve that extends from the descending colon in the left lower quadrant down to the rectum. Its muscular walls feature teniae coli and haustra, which facilitate coordinated peristalsis and stool compaction. The rectum serves as a temporary storage reservoir for fecal waste before defecation. Because the sigmoid colon is mobile and sharply angulated, navigating this anatomical curve during scope insertion requires skill to avoid patient discomfort and mechanical trauma.

headings.title: Equipment and Instrumentation
headings.content:
- **Sigmoidoscope**: Available in rigid metal or flexible fiberoptic variants, though flexible scopes are standard for patient comfort.
- **Light Source and Camera**: Transmits a magnified, high-definition image of the mucosal wall onto a monitor.
- **Insufflation System**: Delivers controlled carbon dioxide or air to distend the bowel lumen for better visibility.
- **Biopsy Forceps**: Specialized tiny instruments passed through the scope channel to harvest tissue samples for histology.
- **Suction Apparatus**: Clears mucus, blood, or residual liquid stool from the optical field.

headings.title: Pre-Procedure Preparation and Assessment
headings.content: Adequate visualization depends entirely on a clean bowel. The nursing staff must verify that bowel preparation protocols—such as sodium picosulfate, clear liquid diets, or cleansing enemas—are completed prior to the procedure. Nurses conduct a baseline physical assessment, review medical history for bleeding disorders or anticoagulant use, check baseline vital signs, and secure written informed consent. Addressing patient anxiety through clear explanations about expected cramping or pressure significantly improves cooperation.

headings.title: Intra-Procedure Nursing Care and Positioning
headings.content: During the procedure, the patient is typically placed in the **left lateral Sims' position**, with knees flexed toward the chest. This posture naturally aligns the sigmoid colon and rectum for smoother scope introduction. The nurse maintains continuous observation of the patient's facial expression, pulse rate, and oxygen saturation. Providing verbal reassurance, managing comfort, and assisting the physician with accessory instruments are core responsibilities during the examination.

headings.title: Post-Procedure Monitoring and Complication Prevention
headings.content: Following the scope withdrawal, patients rest quietly while nurses monitor for delayed complications. Common immediate effects include mild abdominal cramping and flatulence due to retained insufflation gas. Severe abdominal pain, persistent rectal bleeding, fever, or abdominal rigidity signal potential bowel perforation or hemorrhage, requiring immediate surgical notification. Vitals are checked per institutional protocol until the patient is stable.

headings.title: Discharge Instructions and Patient Education
headings.content: Before leaving the facility, patients receive clear instructions regarding normal post-procedural recovery. They are advised that passing small amounts of blood can occur, especially if biopsies were taken, but heavy bleeding or severe pain must be reported immediately. Normal diet and activities can usually be resumed right away. Providing a written summary of warning signs ensures safe home care and timely follow-up for pathology results.
